ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, signatories, and counterparties against the OFAC SDN List and 50% Rule, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Gibraltar Sanctions List maintained under the Sanctions Act 2019, HM Treasury sanctions measures applicable to Gibraltar, and the EU asset freeze lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates; requirements include independent wealth/source-of-funds verification and senior management approval. Screening is continuous on every transaction and rule change, with negative news/adverse media monitoring required under the Gibraltar Money Laundering Regulations 2019 risk-based approach.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry - Official Name Reservation eService, hosted by Her Majesty's Government of Gibraltar (https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/companies-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All statutory filings and company names must be in English using the Latin/Roman alphabet. No transliteration into a local Gibraltar script is required or recognized. The proposed name must be distinguishable from existing names on the register and must end in 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' for a company limited by shares. Non-Latin script names must be normalized to an approved Romanized form before reservation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative objection with the Registrar of Companies within 21 days of the rejection notice, using the standard name appeal form and citing the statutory grounds under section 46 of the Companies Act 2014. The Registrar shall review the objection within 15 business days and issue a written decision. If the administrative appeal fails, the applicant may petition the Supreme Court of Gibraltar for judicial review of the Registrar's decision. A fresh name reservation may be submitted concurrently; a rejection in one class of name does not bar incorporation under a different approved name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A fully virtual office without a physical Gibraltar address cannot satisfy the statutory registered-office obligation. For the contemplated cloud document automation and e-signature SaaS business, a virtual office may be used only as an ancillary administrative address alongside a mandatory physical registered office maintained at a licensed Gibraltar corporate service provider. No trading premises in Gibraltar are required for this non-regulated LegalTech activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low annualized risk, approximately 2% to 4%: no routine unannounced on-site inspection applies to a non-regulated, low-risk LegalTech SaaS company. However, the registered address is subject to periodic due diligence by the licensed corporate service provider, and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission may conduct risk-triggered or complaint-driven unannounced verification visits, particularly where AML/CFT red flags arise.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax); GCT on imports is administered by Gibraltar Customs and Ports Authority. Official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi; income tax e-filing via the eTax portal (etax.gibraltar.gov.gi).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Register the Bermuda Exempted Company as an overseas company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014, filing certified Bermuda certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, directors' register, Gibraltar registered office, and a Gibraltar-resident process agent. 2) Submit the corporate tax registration form to the Income Tax Office (via eTax) with a Bermuda certificate of good standing, a written declaration of place of effective management and control, and the appointed Gibraltar tax agent mandate. 3) The Commissioner issues a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN); non-resident status is acknowledged only after the non-residence declaration is accepted with supporting board-minute and management evidence. 4) Register for GCT with Gibraltar Customs only if physical import of chargeable goods occurs (not triggered by cloud SaaS). 5) If B2C digital services are supplied to UK or EU consumers, additionally register with HMRC as a non-established taxable person for UK VAT and under an EU Member State OSS non-Union scheme.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no check-the-box regime; classification follows statutory management-and-control (POEM) rules. Available mechanisms: (a) non-resident company election by filing a declaration evidencing board control seated in Bermuda, restricting Gibraltar tax to Gibraltar-source income; (b) accounting period election under the Income Tax Act 2010; (c) Gibraltar group relief/surrender election where a GI-resident subsidiary exists; (d) UK-Gibraltar Double Taxation Arrangement (2020) tie-breaker and exchange-of-information procedure; (e) Bermuda Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 opt-in certificate guaranteeing tax exemption in Bermuda until 2035; (f) OSS non-Union and UK VAT registration elections for remote digital supplies.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: General Consumption Tax (GCT) - an import-based goods levy with 0%, 3.5%, 12% and 17% categories; not a VAT. Gibraltar is outside the UK VAT territory, so UK VAT does not apply to Gibraltar domestic supplies. The 2025 announced reform (drafting through 2026) will convert GCT into a broad-based VAT-style tax on supplies of goods and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Current GCT Act: mandatory registration for any person importing chargeable goods in the course of business (no turnover de minimis); proposed GIP 100,000 taxable-supplies threshold under the 2026 reform; UK VAT: zero threshold for non-established suppliers of B2C digital services (NETP registration required from the first onward sale to UK consumers); EU OSS non-Union: no registration threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API e-invoicing or digital stamping mandate is currently in force in Gibraltar. GCT is collected via customs import entries (SAD/GDG documentation). Income tax and PAYE filings are made electronically through eTax. The planned 2026 GCT reform will adopt invoice-based accounting rules but has not announced real-time clearance or API stamping requirements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For the core cloud document automation and e-signature SaaS, no GCT export zero-rating claim is required because exported and offshore digital services fall wholly outside the current GCT charge. For UK and EU VAT, B2B supplies are outside the scope of the supplier with the recipient applying reverse charge; B2C digital supplies require supplier VAT registration and output VAT at destination rates (UK 20% via HMRC NETP; EU rates via OSS non-Union). The 2026 GCT reform intends to keep exported services and cross-border B2B services outside charge or zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/GDG entry) - required only for physical goods movements; not applicable to pure cloud services
Commercial contract and e-signature authentication/audit logs evidencing service delivery to overseas counterparties
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / Stripe payout statements evidencing foreign-source receipts
Customer VAT/GST/TIN credentials and B2B/B2C status declarations supporting reverse charge or OSS treatment
Bermuda certificate of good standing and Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966 certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Gibraltar: misdeclaration of residence or false exemption claims trigger assessments without time limits in fraud cases, interest, a civil penalty of up to 100% of underdeclared tax, and criminal prosecution (unlimited fine and up to 7 years' imprisonment) under the Income Tax Act 2010 and GCT Act. UK HMRC: non-established VAT penalties up to 30-100% with repayment claims subject to mitigation and recharacterisation risk if UK substance is found. Bermuda: Economic Substance Act 2019 penalties up to BMD 250,000 and 6 years' imprisonment for substance or filing failures; the tax-exempt status and Tax Protection Act 1966 certificate may be retrospectively clawed back if management and control indicators (board meetings, IP decision-making, staff) are not maintained in Bermuda.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) for exchange-control oversight of the Bermuda Exempted Company; Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) for licensing and FX conduct supervision within Gibraltar.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Bermuda Exempted Company, when designated non-resident under Bermuda's Exchange Control Act 1972, enjoys unrestricted convertibility for both capital and current account transactions. Gibraltar operates a free capital movement environment; the Gibraltar pound (GIP) is pegged 1:1 with GBP and freely convertible. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repatriation require no exchange-control approval, but intermediaries apply standard AML/CFT transaction verification and source-of-wealth checks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory foreign-exchange surrender timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies. As a non-resident designated Bermuda Exempted Company, the entity may retain export proceeds in any permitted currency and is not subject to the 6-month repatriation requirement reserved for resident entities. In Gibraltar, there are no surrender rules; funds may be kept, converted, or swept offshore at the holder's discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Treasury Sweep Account
Capital Escrow Account / Private Banking Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for a GFSC-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) offering multi-currency accounts and local IBANs. Legal constraints: a non-EEA EMI (e.g., UK, Malta or Cyprus authorised) cannot passport automatically into Gibraltar post-Brexit; a Gibraltar branch or top-up licence is required to hold client funds locally. The Bermuda Exempted Company may board on an offshore EMI (e.g., Wise Platform or Torchange) only if the EMI's entity-acceptance policy tolerates holding offshore companies in low-risk jurisdictions; most require physical substance evidence and a 'no negative news' historical profile. Overall viability: Medium-High, with regulatory-minimum EMI onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar banks, acting under GFSC AML/CFT guidance, generally mandate a physical interview for at least one natural person with actual control (typically a director) and all beneficial owners above threshold. Remote opening is permitted only when the applicant uses a registered Gibraltar corporate service provider as introducer, combined with certified copy legalisation, live video identification and independent electronic ID verification; in practice, for offshore Bermuda Exempted Companies, almost all tier-1 banks require an in-person interview at a Gibraltar office or at a law-firm's office as a delegatee of the bank. Non-negotiable: original passport, board resolution, and certificate of good standing must be produced.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore jurisdiction nexus — Bermuda Exempted Company with no tax residency and low effective substance in Gibraltar.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a substance profile evidencing (i) a physical office in Gibraltar with lease; (ii) two or more Gibraltar-resident directors; (iii) board meeting minutes held in Gibraltar; (iv) outsourcing agreements proving local management of sales, support, and treasury functions; (v) UK/Gibraltar tax residence assessment (for the company or its management) and economic substance return filings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholders or bearer shares; beneficial ownership opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a registered beneficial ownership register with ultimate natural persons, trust deed (where any corporate shareholder is a trust), beneficial ownership declaration form, and source-of-wealth statements supported by audited investment or business income documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border subscription receipts from unrelated SaaS consumers without a physical local merchant presence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide signed master subscription agreements, Stripe standard merchant agreement, payment processor board resolution, ISAE 3402 SOC 2 Type II report, and a documented business model note explaining digital-only sales, local and overseas sales channels, and absence of cash-intensive operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires the investor to send the wire in accordance with operational purpose codes. Use SWIFT MT103 with the Interbank Message Type 'INCREASE OF SUBSCRIBED CAPITAL' in the purpose field; require the remitter to include the entity's tax reference (Gibraltar Company Number or GNF) in field 70 (Remittance Information). The receiving bank shall obtain a Certified Capital Injection Instruction endorsed by the Board; the audited statement of the parent must show the capital injection. For Bermuda exchange-control, file a non-resident status notification with BMA; for Gibraltar, report the inward remittance in the annual financial returns if it qualifies as foreign direct investment; no prior approval is required unless the bank flags a source-of-funds anomaly.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service trade settlements (license fees, cloud hosting, HR payroll, professional fees), the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 international transfers for EUR/USD/GBP, supported by SEPA Instant for EUR-only accounts where applicable. Commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) are permissible but operationally unnecessary for SaaS/service contracts; instead, use SWIFT MT103 with fixed reference to the underlying invoice. For subscription merchant payouts and refunds, Stripe routes via Visa/Mastercard clearing rails (STP rails) into the designated operational bank account; ensure clearance through the same entity's account to avoid third-party settlement risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright foreign exchange forward contracts with GFSC-licensed or UK/FCA-authorized counterparties
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for inconvertible or restricted currencies (e.g., INR, TRY, BRL) with settlement in USD/GBP/EUR
Exchange-traded FX futures and options (CME Group or ICE)
Plain-vanilla FX options for subscription price hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return and Annual Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January; first period prorated from incorporation to the next 31 January; fee tier determined by authorized share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a default penalty and a surcharge on the unpaid annual government fee; persistent non-payment for more than three months after written notice permits the Registrar to strike the company off the Bermuda Register and dissolve it.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Register Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda (confidential beneficial ownership register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation, and within 30 days after any registerable change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is a statutory offence subject to monetary penalties; false or misleading beneficial-ownership information carries further fines; prolonged default can result in restriction, administrative strike-off and deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies / Tax Commissioner via the Economic Substance Act filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within six months after the end of the financial year; applicable where the exempted company carries on a relevant activity in Bermuda
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: First contravention attracts a penalty of BMD 1,000; subsequent contraventions attract penalties up to BMD 10,000 plus daily default fines; non-compliance with economic substance requirements may also expose the company to information exchange and strike-off action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar Overseas Company Annual Return and Filed Accounts (required if the Bermuda Exempted Company is registered in Gibraltar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Gibraltar Companies Registry / Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of the overseas-company registration in Gibraltar; accounts must be filed with the return or within nine months of the financial year-end as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing gives rise to daily default fines; failure to remedy within three months after Gazette notice enables the Registrar to strike off the Gibraltar registration and dissolve the branch presence.

stage_6.form_identifier_and_portal: Gibraltar Companies Annual Corporate Tax Return (ITO CT Return) filed via the Gibraltar Income Tax Office (ITO) online e-filing service; a copy is also retained under s.70 of the Income Tax Act 2010.
stage_6.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 10 months after the end of the company's accounting period (e.g., for 31 December year-end, filing due by 31 October of the following year).
